title: The Rise of Open Models in the Enterprise — Amir Haghighat, Baseten
talk_summary: A Baseten co-founder describes why enterprises move from closed frontier APIs to self-hosted open models: task-specific fine-tunes beat generic models, latency and unit economics break down under agentic workloads, and shared APIs optimize throughput over tail latency. Most of the talk is about the operational burden of running inference yourself (speculative decoding, prefix caching, disaggregated serving, failover, autoscaling).

takeaways.technique: Agentic call amplification as the real cost driver
takeaways.what_they_do: They frame cost blowups as a consequence of agentic loops multiplying inference calls per user action, which invalidates the 'price per token will keep falling' assumption.
takeaways.evidence_quote: every single user action can result in literally 50 inference calls

takeaways.technique: Task-specific models beat frontier generalists on narrow tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: Enterprises with labeled data fine-tune or self-host small models for narrow extraction/transcription tasks where generic frontier models underperform.

takeaways.technique: Prefix caching and disaggregated serving for agentic prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: They note agentic workloads have large but highly similar prompts, so prefix caching and prefill/decode disaggregation materially improve time-to-first-token and P99.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the prompts are massive but the prompts are somewhat similar from one to the other

takeaways.technique: Tail-latency and failover discipline for self-hosted serving
takeaways.what_they_do: They describe how crashes of the serving stack (vLLM/Triton) spike tail latency while replicas restart, and that naive replica bring-up takes minutes, breaking burst handling.
takeaways.evidence_quote: when Triton crashes often your tail latencies go through the roof while you wait for these things to come back
takeaways.numbers: 8 minutes to bring up a new replica of the same model

takeaways.what_they_do: Shared APIs are tuned for high QPS at the expense of latency; latency-critical paths need different serving choices.
takeaways.evidence_quote: inherently they're optimized for high throughput and high QPS at the expense of latency
